title: We Now Know What Denisovans Looked Like - Nautilus
gist: A Nature study by Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers used proteomic sequencing on 20 fossils (~130,000 years old) from Xujiayao to identify them as Denisovan, putting a face to the archaic hominin.

insights.claim: Denisovans were identified as a genetically distinct hominin line only in the past 15 years, though fossils were found nearly half a century ago.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shows how recent the field's key discoveries are.
insights.locator: While fossils from these archaic hominins

insights.claim: Chinese Academy of Sciences researchers studied about 20 Xujiayao fossils dating to roughly 130,000 years ago, excavated in the 1970s and previously unassigned to a hominin group.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Old collections can be reclassified with new methods.
insights.locator: A team of paleoanthropologists and geneticists

insights.claim: Proteomic sequencing of collagen peptides found an amino acid substitution unique to Denisovans and absent in humans and Neanderthals, assigning the Xujiayao fossils to Denisovans.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Protein analysis can classify fossils where DNA is unavailable.
